accuracy: Distances are 1/parallax with no prior (Gaia DR3 for 98% of rows). Positions are J2000.0, J1991.25 for a few Hipparcos-only stars. The Gaia parallaxes inside AT-HYG come from ESA/Gaia/DPAC, whose own licence could not be read from this network: a downloaded third-party package states CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO, Celestia and celestia-gaia-stardb files state CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO, and the AWS registry says "Attribution required". Treat the Gaia-derived values as non-commercial until confirmed. AT-HYG's ACKNOWLEDGMENTS omit SIMBAD and Tycho-2 although its build notes use both; they are credited here.
adaptations: Positions converted to ICRS Cartesian parsecs from ra/dec/dist; V derived from Tycho VT as V = VT - 0.090 (BT-VT) (the formula in AT-HYG's own build notes) for 209908 rows; absolute magnitudes recomputed as V + 5 - 5 log10 d without extinction correction; colours turned into display temperatures; 209156 stars within 500 pc with parallax/error > 10 packed into deep.bin (pc x 64 in int16, M_V in 0.1 mag steps). The shipped files stay under CC BY-SA 4.0.
licence_quote: "This work is licensed under a [Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License][cc-by-sa]." (LICENSE)
source: Compiled from Tycho-2 (Høg et al. 2000) and its first supplement, Hipparcos (ESA 1997; van Leeuwen 2007 reduction via HYG), Gaia DR3 and DR2 parallaxes (ESA/Gaia/DPAC, through gaiadr3.gaia_source_lite and SIMBAD look-ups), the Yale Bright Star Catalog, the Gliese & Jahreiss 1991 nearby-star catalogue, the Tycho-2 Spectral Type Catalog (Wright et al. 2003) and SIMBAD cross-identifications.
title: AT-HYG v3.2 (Augmented Tycho-HYG), subsets athyg_32_reduced_m10 and athyg_32_hyg_ids

accuracy: Gliese 1991 distances are often photometric: for Gliese-only stars within 20 pc that AT-HYG matched to Gaia DR3, 72% agree within 20% and 5% are off by more than a factor of two (measured on these files).
adaptations: Used for the 661 HYG rows AT-HYG does not carry: Gliese companions (placed at their primary's AT-HYG distance along their own direction, flag bit 2) and Gliese-only stars (at their Gliese 1991 distance, flag bit 6); spectral types filled for 971 and B-V for 0 AT-HYG rows that had none; HIP 55203 (xi UMa, deleted in HYG v3.5) mapped to HYG's xi UMa A.
licence_quote: "The licensing for HYG v4.0 is Creative Commons CC BY-SA 4.0, unlike previous versions of the HYG catalog." (hyg/version-info.md)
source: Hipparcos (ESA 1997, 2007 new reduction), Yale Bright Star Catalog 5th ed. (Hoffleit 1991), Gliese & Jahreiss 1991 (CNS3 preliminary); IAU WGSN names.
title: HYG database v4.1 (hygdata_v41.csv)

accuracy: Parallax quantised to 0.02 mas; the catalogue author calls the files experimental.
adaptations: Nothing shipped. Each AT-HYG star was joined by Gaia DR3 id or HIP number to read its parallax error. The error qualifies AT-HYG's distance only when both come from the same Gaia DR3 source (332286 rows) or when Stellarium's parallax agrees with it within 3 sigma (1733 rows).
licence: No data licence stated; the files ship in a GPL-2.0-or-later source tree
licence_quote: COPYING: "GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 2, June 1991"; no data-specific notice.
owner: Stellarium team; catalogues built by Henry Leung (henrysky/stellarium_star_catalogs)
source: Gaia DR3 (ESA/Gaia/DPAC) and Hipparcos/XHIP values via SIMBAD
title: Stellarium v26.2 hip_gaia3 star catalogues 0-3 (build-time filter only)

accuracy: Figures are a drawing convention, not a measurement; IAU constellations are defined by their boundaries.
adaptations: 752 unique figure segments resolved to named rows (30 touch a star with no usable parallax and are kept only for the sky view); 525 IAU names attached.
source: Constellation figures from the IAU "The Constellations" pages (Sky & Telescope: Roger Sinnott, Rick Fienberg, Alan MacRobert); star names from the IAU Catalog of Star Names (IAU WGSN).
title: Stellarium v26.2 sky culture "modern_iau"

accuracy: Catalogue as of the pinned commit; not complete (e.g. no planet listed for Barnard's Star; eps Eridani b is "Controversial" and so not shown).
adaptations: Planets with list "Confirmed planets" only (1255 planets on 889 named rows); hosts joined to AT-HYG/HYG by identifier (828) or position (36); 167 hosts placed from the catalogue's own coordinates and distance.
licence_quote: "The database is licensed under an MIT license (see below), which basically says you can do everything with it." (README.md)
source: Community-curated compilation (Rein 2012, arXiv:1211.7121); recent entries imported from the NASA Exoplanet Archive.
title: Open Exoplanet Catalogue

accuracy: Dwarf sequence applied to all luminosity classes; display use only.
adaptations: Bt-Vt and spectral-type columns interpolated to effective temperature for display colours; only the derived colour table ships.
licence: No licence stated on the table (MeanStars code: BSD-3-Clause)

accuracy: Blackbody-based model; underestimates hot stars (B-V -0.2 gives ~13,600 K).
adaptations: T = T0 (1/(a BV + b) + 1/(a BV + c)) with {'a': 0.92, 'b': 1.7, 'c': 0.62, 'T0': 4600.0}; a model, labelled as one.
owner: F. J. Ballesteros; coefficients as coded in PyAstronomy 0.25.0 (MIT)
title: B-V to effective temperature relation (Ballesteros 2012, EPL 97, 34008)

accuracy: Chromaticity of an ideal blackbody; real stellar spectra differ, especially for M stars.
adaptations: Planck spectra integrated against the CMFs, converted with the IEC 61966-2-1 sRGB matrix, normalised to the largest channel.
